I've had 3x appointments with 3x different consultants at this clinic, but every time I left feeling like I'm not taken seriously. There seems little internal communication. I need to chase referrals and when I went for a skin biopsy the surgeon wasn't aware of the actual procedure she had to perform on me as her colleague did not inform her. The consultants always seem in a hurry. They do not take the time to answer questions (instead they repudiate them) or carefully listen, which results in being misinformed about treatments and "new"  information being brought to the table from my end during each different consultation. My concerns, questions and requests for specific treatments are ushered away and I am constantly being told to visit other specialists to look at my skin condition. In short, I am not happy at all. I appreciate my condition may be hard to diagnose, but I feel like the consultants at this clinic don't even try to help.

Updated - The clinic has apologised and asked me to remove my review. I haven't and, as a result, they refuse to treat me at the clinic in the future.

Horrible staff, horrible doctor and horrible experience.  We booked with Dr. Laura Proudfoot, and we’re deeply disappointed with the very poor “NHS Style” service at Private medical cost. We spend over £600 for a basic treatment and the treatment was far from being effective.  We were told at the appointment that the doctor will redo the procedure if it was ineffective, but on the day of the follow-up appointment she called and cancelled the appointment via her assistant, and said we should consult a surgeon and she can’t help us and does not understand the issue.  The least a doctor can do is make an assessment and provide her professional opinion during the appointment, instead of leaving a message for her patient that she doesn’t want to see us anymore. That is very unprofessional and unethical for a medical professional.  I am a doctor and would never treat my patients in that manner.

On top of the the front office staff is just horrible at treating the patients with respect.  Both times at the clinic the staff was rude and unpleasant.

I hope the learn and improve their service and I truly don’t understand how this place got even 3 stars on google reviews.

leads.Review Text: The doctor I saw a couple months back Dr Richard Coelho was very hurried and spent only 5-7 mins for an expensive appointment and prescribed a cream which didn’t work. I overlooked the fact he was hurried and thought I’d give a second chance and see the same doctor again. Today I came for a follow up appointment and I changed a flight to make the appointment. Guess what? They cancelled their appointment for me with zero notice and claimed they sent an email on the 30th Aug 2022 which purported to say that I needed to pay in advance and since it was not paid the appointment was cancelled. I told them that the last time I attended I paid on the day for the first appointment so what’s changed? They said they changed their policy six months ago (my first appointment was about 2 months ago so that’s not true). When I pulled up the same said email they sent me on the 30th Aug 2022 I showed them the email and it said nothing of the sort about having to prepay before an appointment. She then said sorry the wrong email has been sent to me in error. The receptionist then attempted to speak to the doctor to see if they could fit me in. The doctor said he couldn’t and didn’t care that I’d changed a flight at my expense to make the appointment. There are other better dermatology clinics in London. Avoid this one unless you want an unprofessional service and be messed around and have your time wasted.

It just seemed they wanted the money and wouldn’t even face you to say the case was beyond their capabilities and suggest a proper specialist ( as any good doctor would do).

I had a very disappointing experience with SKN Clinics and want to warn potential customers.
In late June, I contacted them to ask about laser treatments for thread veins. I explained on the phone that I only wanted an informal chat to understand what options were available, as I wasn’t sure whether I would go ahead with treatment. I was told this could be arranged with a £50 refundable deposit, which would either be returned if I didn’t proceed or used towards treatment if I did. That sounded reasonable, so I booked.
A few days before the appointment, I checked their website and noticed consultations were listed at £180, with a cancellation policy requiring 5 days’ notice. Concerned, I called to clarify. At that point, I was told I had actually been booked for a full consultation — not the brief chat I was originally promised — and that I would be charged £180 if I went ahead. I was also told I had lost my £50 deposit since I was now within the 5-day cancellation window. None of this was made clear during my first call.
On July 1st, I raised a complaint with a helpful staff member (Christopher Hopkins), who agreed I had been misled and assisted me with filing it. On July 2nd, I received an email confirming the matter would be resolved within 20 days. As of August 23rd, I have heard nothing further.
This experience has left me feeling misled and ignored. If this is how SKN Clinics handle a small issue, I dread to think how they might deal with something more serious. I strongly suggest looking elsewhere. For example, I later went to Cavendish Clinics in John Lewis, where the consultation and patch test were both free, and the treatment itself was only £90.

Based on the interaction, the fact they are lower-rated than other clinics in the area, doesn't surprise me.

I will say, however, I think I spoke to someone at their call centre and not the clinic itself.

The first time I went for a consultation, one receptionist groaned to the other.
I didn't feel welcomed and couldn't understand what was wrong.
I later found out the doctor was running late and I was told his train had been late. When I asked how late I was informed that he was running half an hour late. I was unable to wait for my appointment so it was rearranged for 2 weeks later.

I received the test patch and my leg is very  badly bruised. I realised it might bruise but I'm unsure if it's usual to be bruised so badly.
I felt the clinic was too busy, overheard someone complaining about her treatment and the doctor seemed stressed.
I have cancelled my next appointment as I have no confidence in this clinic.
It appeared chaotic and disorganised. I had a long wait on the phone to cancel and couldn't find how to cancel on the website. It certainly wasn't apparent.
An expensive trial and  a very poor service for a potential new patient.
I will now search for a more professional clinic.

am writing to express my deep frustration and disappointment regarding the recent consultation I had with one of your doctors. What I experienced was not only unprofessional, but could have had serious — and potentially life-threatening — consequences.

I booked the appointment urgently, concerned about a lesion on my arm that I feared might be skin cancer. However, instead of examining the area, the doctor spent over 20 minutes discussing a genetic screening program — something he was clearly trying to sell to both me and my wife. This was not the reason for my visit, and the focus on this program was both inappropriate and distressing at a time when I was extremely anxious about my health.

It was only after my wife directly asked him if he was going to look at my arm that he finally did — with only a few minutes left in the appointment. He diagnosed it as eczema and prescribed a steroid cream, which the pharmacy couldn’t even read due to the poor handwriting.

Since then, I received an urgent appointment through the NHS, where the lesion was surgically removed. It turned out to contain cancerous cells. I have now lost a significant portion of my arm due to the delay in treatment. The NHS consultant who treated me even commented, "He can’t be much of a doctor if he thought that was eczema."

I will not be paying for this consultation and have lodged a formal complaint with Bupa, requesting they withhold their contribution as well. I also intend to share my experience publicly to warn others.

This experience left me frightened, angry, and let down at a time when I needed professional medical help. The service I received was unacceptable and potentially dangerous.

I expect this matter to be taken seriously and investigated thoroughly.

During my recent visit to the clinic, I inadvertently used my business card to settle payment for a treatment. Upon recognizing this error, I promptly contacted the clinic to rectify the situation. I offered to make a payment using my personal credit card and requested a refund for the initial payment made with the business card, which was agreed upon by the clinic staff. Subsequently, I made another payment using my personal credit card.

Despite providing the long card number of the business card I mistakenly used for the initial payment, the clinic staff denied that it was the card used and refused to process the refund. I later received an email from the clinic with an account number that did not correspond to any of my accounts. I replied to the email clarifying this and provided evidence of the payment from my business bank statement, yet this was not accepted by the clinic.

I further offered to visit the clinic in person with my phone and bank statement to resolve the issue, but this offer was declined. Faced with the clinic's refusal to refund the erroneously charged amount, I proceeded to contact my bank to initiate a chargeback.

Following this, I received a call from the clinic's finance department, where I was informed that using Apple Pay displays a different number than the physical card. I also confirmed this information with Apple Support. I assumed the clinic's finance department would relay this information internally, but it seems that communication was lacking.

Subsequently, I received an email asking me to make a payment, and upon calling the clinic in good faith to settle the matter, I was met with continued denial of the card used for payment. Despite explaining the situation to the Clinic Manager, I encountered a refusal to acknowledge the error or offer an apology.

The lack of understanding regarding Apple Pay on the clinic's part, coupled with their unwillingness to consider alternative explanations for the discrepancy, has led to significant inconvenience, distress, and wasted time. The absence of an apology for their mistake is disappointing, and I urge the clinic to address their operational shortcomings and provide better customer service in the future…

Thank you for acknowledging the feedback. Regrettably, contrary to your assertion, there was no commitment made by you during our last call. You continued to assert that the card number I provided did not match the one used for payment. There was a lack of acknowledgment of the mistake made by you or an apology from your end. As mentioned during our last call, I have already consulted with the clinic's finance department, who confirmed the discrepancy related to Apple Pay. Therefore, I am uncertain why you are stating that your finance department will be contacting me. It appears that you are not fully acknowledging my feedback!

I contacted Louise who carried out my treatments. I explained that after 4 months the filler hadnt gone down, not even a little bit. I'd decided I would like for it to be dissolved (which had been previously offered, at no cost).

I had a reply back saying she (Louise) wouldnt do it for 'a number of reasons' that she'd discussed with management.

She didnt elaborate other than saying she didnt want to because I'd previously been disappointed with her standard of work. She basically said I can go elsewhere (at cost to myself)

I had spoken with two other clinicians prior to emailing who said that a good therapist would always try to correct any work that went wrong (even after 4 months) so I am genuinely surprised to have recieved a no.

Apparently I've been passed to the practice manager so we will see how that pans out and I will update accordingly.

I initially went along just for  some botox in my frown lines and 11s. We obviously got chatting and Louise brought up filler as an option. I said I hadn't considered it because I'd heard so many horror stories.

Louise told me it's a really low risk and I would be a perfect candidate and that I'd have "amazing results" I wished I'd gone with my gut. I was lulled into this false sense of security. I'm not saying that it was done in an intentional or manipulative way but thats what happened.

I said yes to the filler (tear trough) so I had that and also the botox.

Immediately afterwards it didn't look too bad. My frown lines were already going and the filler looked OK.

However the very next day I looked awful. You could see the filler protruding under my eyes and even my frown lines were starting to come back.

I went in for a botox top up a couple of weeks later. I mentioned the filler and Louise said I needed to give it time (it had been 2 weeks by then)

Whilst there I also had profhilo as Louise said it would tighten my face and smoothe out the wrinkles and blemishes (particularly the lines above my lip)

I went away and again the frown lines returned. Pretty much all were back by day 4.
Within a month I could see no affect from the profhilo but I'd been told that's normal and the results will come immediately after treatment 2.

I had treatment number 2 about 4-5 weeks after the 1st one. I'm now about 6 week's post treatment 2 and honestly it's had no affect. I still have all of my lines and blemishes and redness (I was told this would all even out)

The filler still looks horrendous. I have been in constant contact with the clinic telling them how awful it is.

I was called back in for higher strength botox (no charge) and I'm a week past that now and the results are ok.

Under my eyes look terrible though. I look completely weird when I smile and the filler has caused weird bumps.

I spent about £1500 in total and all I have to show for it is a relatively smooth forehead. Oh and a messed up face. I can't even leave the house without glasses as my confidence is on the floor.

I went along for treatments to treat myself. I'm a disabled single parent of a disabled child.  I wanted to do something for myself to make me feel better/more refreshed.

I'm left feeling that I've basically paid for someone to ruin my face. That was a large sum of money to me. I saved for 3months just to afford some treatments for self care purposes.

The only option now re the filler is to have it dissolved. I can't go down that route as its dangerous, I've seen so so many stories about how bad dissolving it can be.

I'm extremely disappointed and unbelievably sad  that I've been left feeling this way.

I’m not one for writing bad reviews, especially given how difficult it has been for businesses during the pandemic. However the quality of care I received after a failed laser attempt at my birthmark removal was beyond poor. First of all, they are impossible to get hold of - I understand this has been challenging because they have been incredibly busy and they have since hired more staff. Maybe things are different now… Secondly, there is NO aftercare post-procedure. This does not bode well with not being able to contact them especially when you are concerned the wound is becoming infected.

I eventually managed to speak to someone from the head office and was called into southampton for another doctor to investigate. This doctor advised strongly against CO2RE lasering for my birthmark (a congenital mole) because of concerns with skin cancer. I was very shocked and extremely concerned that this was not raised to me during my initial consultation. I personally felt like I had not been fully informed about the process was left feeling confused. In actual fact, I cried my eyes out while in the clinic due to feeling misinformed and nobody ever contacted me after to apologise or explain anything. So then I tried to arrange a meeting to discuss this issue several weeks back and have had no reply from anyone at the southampton clinic.

I am so disappointed with this whole process because birthmark removal is a huge decision to make and it is also very expensive. To my knowledge, birthmark removal is the most complex treatment they offer, so you’d think more care and time would be put into the process? I’m also disappointed to have spent £100 on an initial consultation that clearly was not informing me of important details.

As a result, I would not recommend this skn clinic.

I'm extremely disappointed with the laser skin treatment service. I've been a client for 2 years, having multiple treatments, including my recent micro-needling session.

The 1st session showed great results and gave my skin a nice glow. After 6 weeks, I booked a 2nd session, but it didn't go well. My skin's become really dry, and I haven't seen any improvement.

I complained, but it led to follow-up meetings and lengthy explanations that didn't fix my skin. I'm dissatisfied and disappointed. They don't seem to acknowledge the issue.

They claim 2nd-time results never match the first, but isn't that why they recommend multiple sessions?

I've attached pics of both treatments, and it's clear the 1st session had better results. I'm not seeing any difference before and after the 2nd session 😕.

So think twice before you book for your session . Not every team member well trained .

I feel quite disappointed in the customer service here. I booked online and went in for my treatment on the same day (which was great!). However, my appointment time was looming and can't just pop to West Quay last minute, due to the drive in taking some time. I was still awaiting confirmation that my treatment could go ahead, so had to phone in to get the confirmation that I should have received via email.

The treatment itself was okay; not much support to make the experience comfortable. It felt a bit rushed and, from my perspective, I thought I saw some smirking looks directed towards me when I was discussing my body (however, of course that is just my perspective...). But the treatment was fine overall and results lasted a couple weeks.

After my treatment, I went to the main reception to book some treatments again. I did not feel listened to at all. I verbalised the treatments I wanted, but the staff kept selecting the wrong ones on their system/selecting the incorrect number of treatments requested and the price kept going up. So I had to continue correcting them and repeating the desired (intimate) treatments in a busy waiting room. Furthermore, they kept reading out what I wanted/what they kept trying to book me in for (against my request,) out loud. This all felt quite embarrassing, considering the busyness. I do wonder if she was trying to book me in for additional treatments just to get more money from me... I think, if she had her own recommendations and considerations for what I might like and how many treatments, surely this could have been discussed with me before she tried booking me in for them without explanation?? And in the treatment room before I went out to rebook, to avoid such a discussion in front of strangers?

The lady serving me requested support from the manager, which was all fine and done to support me in booking my treatments, which was good of her. But he did not address me at all. He just spoke to the other staff about what I wanted e.g. "what does the lady want?". I felt slightly frustrated over this, as booking in again appeared far more complex than I think it should have been. Though perhaps he had his own anxieties around customer service and struggled to look at me/interact with me directly... who knows!

In OCTOBER, I had to cancel my second appointment due to an unexpected family emergency. I have been trying to contact the clinic since, in order to rebook. I've heard nothing. I have paid for the treatments already, too. Feels like all they care for is money and not supporting their customers to feel more confident in their bodies, and offering a positive, client-centred service. I work Mon-Fri and weekends are typically busy for me, so don't have the opportunity to go to West Quay often, just to go into the store to ask where the responses to my contact attempts are!

Please can somebody get back to me about the incomplete treatments I have paid for, and when I might be able to rebook. It's been three+ months now.

If I could rate this much lower, I would. It is unfortunate that I’m having to leave a negative review but this incident was not dealt with professionally or at all for that matter. First, I’m aware this review will receive a negative response from the owner of this clinic like almost all of the 1 stars reviews they’ve received and they have shown in numerous occasions that they are always right and anything else is unacceptable. I’d like to clarify that I’ve not had any issues with my previous appointments except from the fact that I literally have a new laser ‘therapist’ in almost every single appointment I’ve had with them so privacy or consistency for intimate areas is out the window. High staff turnover should’ve been a red flag already and even if I requested the same person to do my appointment, this would not have been possible.

My most recent experience resulted in my right eyebrow being burnt. When I contacted them about this, the owner Joe picked up the phone and it sounded like he didn’t know what I expected them to do about this. I informed them to ask for advice and he asked for me to send an email with pictures as I was unable to go in to have them look at it due to work commitments. I felt it was only right to inform them of a mistake that the therapist had made and it was fair to request a refund to rectify this. I didn’t hear back from them till almost a week later. After my appointment, I started to feel sensitivity and soreness all over my face (specifically, the areas that had laser hair removal). I gave them the benefit of the doubt because this was a treatment that involved laser therefore SOME discomfort is to be expected but is rare. This went on for days and became progressively worse. My face because painfully sore, it looked dry and also looked like my skin was sagging. The affected areas felt very warm to touch and would continue like this for literally days. It was red and was the most intense discomfort I’ve ever felt on my face. I couldn’t clean it like before or put anything else on it. I didn’t hear back from them until I pushed for an update. I asked my GP and other laser clinics for advice because I didn’t hear back from them and I was very concerned and anxious about my face. Both confirmed my face was burnt by the laser. When the owner finally got in touch, they were ‘concerned’ that I had gotten in touch with another clinic. They asked me multiple times to come to the clinic even AFTER I’ve explained to them how anxious I was due to mistake they caused. I sent them very detailed description and MULTIPLE pictures for reference. There was no accountability on their end and not even an ounce of empathy or respect when spoken to on the phone. This back and forth went on for almost a month. All I requested for was a refund for that specific treatment. I didn’t receive this and they have stopped replying. I could not emphasise enough the distress this caused and even the impact it had on my confidence. All before and after care were followed as they advised. A new laser therapist was doing my appointment that day. I did nothing different before or after my appointment, including any changes to my face wash, moisturiser etc. My biggest advice to you - READ THE 1 STAR REVIEWS AND DO NOT COME HERE.

I paid up front in bulk for 8 sessions of underarms, Brazilian and full legs. My first two appointments with Jodie and Holly (I think) were great.
Next I had 4 appointments with Shima - everytime she would say “you’ve been tanning” and point to my legs, to which I would reply “nope, any tan lines I have are from July” she would reply “hmm” in a way which made me feel like I was being called a liar. She refused to do my feet and toes, she said this was not included in full legs, absolutely fine if this is true but she was the only person who said this.  I have had 8 session and my feet and toes have only been done 4 times. I then had a blonde lady who was really lovely and thorough on all areas!
My last appointment was with Aga who completely rushed my appointment. This was the only session I flinched because of the pain, of which she almost laughed and said “only a few more”, on my Brazilian she didn’t  use the wooden sticks to get into all the areas. The day after my skin was purple and is now yellow which looks like bruising - photos attached. Disappointed that only 3 out of 8 sessions were to a great standard after travelling all the way from Portsmouth every 4 weeks.

Unless you are in the top 10% income bracket, stay away from this place! You will be scammed. My 20-minute appointment ended up costing me half of my salary. Initially, I was informed that the visit with the gynecologist would be £200. However, during my 20-minute appointment, I was offered a scan and an endometrial biopsy without any mention of additional costs or their amounts.

To my shock, the total bill was £560 – the biopsy cost £200, the scan was £100, and the appointment itself was £260. I was heartbroken and felt truly cheated. There was no transparency about the pricing, and I was left with an exorbitant bill. I strongly advise against visiting this clinic unless you have money to spare.
